stemMd: Which principle most closely guides the passage?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Future interpretations should be prevented from differing.

options.label: B
options.textMd: All physical alteration is equally harmful.

options.label: C
options.textMd: An interpretation should not obscure the evidence needed to evaluate or revise it.

options.label: D
options.textMd: An attractive display matters more than a documented one.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The earliest version of an object is always the only authentic one.

explanationMd: The closing sentence states the guiding concern: interpretation must not silently replace evidence. Documentation and reversibility operationalize that concern by allowing later evaluation rather than locking the object to one account.

distractorRationale.e: The chair's later life challenges that principle.
distractorRationale.d: The passage gives documentation a central role.
